title: Canonical open restriction on augmented quotient models
statement: Fix independent site and coefficient universes, a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, and an open immersion j:U→X. Use the section-normalized coefficient transports and exact open operations o of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let SU and SX be the actual strict-system reduction/total-limit calculi of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Supply the ordinary generator-normalized tensor comparison and an ambient extension comparison r represented on all flat-term K-flat complexes by simultaneous augmented quotient presentations and their canonical extension tensor maps. Then the mate of r inverse under the actual open and system adjunctions is an isomorphism. This isomorphism has, on every flat-term K-flat complex on X, one strict chain-isomorphism representative between the restricted quotient systems, with both augmented presentations and with finite components the actual finite-adjunction mate of the inverse ordinary tensor comparison.

proof.text: Restrict a flat-term K-flat representative and each quotient tensor on the localized ringed site. Exact restriction preserves good representatives. The ordinary restriction/tensor map keeps each pure tensor. Its inverse is the same sectionwise identification, transported through the fixed coefficient equivalences. Thus the degreewise maps are chain isomorphisms, commute with quotient transitions and scalar units, and form one strict system isomorphism.

proof.text: Localize these natural chain isomorphisms on the resolving class. For an extension summand [x] tensor a, its adjunct is the inverse supplied extension tensor map followed by the ordinary counit. The augmented extension models in the hypothesis identify this with r inverse; the same equality holds on strict system sections before localization. The derived open adjunction therefore identifies the resulting natural isomorphism with mateEquiv applied to r inverse. The finite component is exactly the unit/inverse-tensor/counit formula in the statement.

      (κC : ∀ n : ℕ,

      (r.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) ≫ (J l E j o).map eC.hom ≫
        (systemExtension l E j o).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app C =
      SX.reduction.map ((extension l E j o).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app Q) ≫
        eD.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map f.hom) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ),
        (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n).map (f.hom.f i) ≫
          (extensionEvaluation l E j o n).hom.app (C.X i) ≫
          (finiteExtension l E j o n).map ((κC n).hom.f i) =
        (κD n).hom.f i ≫ (tensor.ordinary n).hom.app (Q.X i))) :

      (CU : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E U) ℤ)

      (κU : ∀ n : ℕ,

      AugmentedPresentation l E X SX Q CX eX κX ∧
      CoefficientReductionPresentation l E U SU.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
        (((restriction l E j o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) hRes.1 CU eU κU ∧
      AugmentedPresentation l E U SU
        (((restriction l E j o).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) CU eU κU ∧
      (SU.reduction.map ((restriction l E j o).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app Q) ≫

      s.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) ≫ (P l E j o).map eX.hom ≫
        (systemRestriction l E j o).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app CX) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ),

    (o.finite n).inverse.mapIso ((o.openSystems.restrictionEvaluation n).app (CX.X i))).hom ≫

        (κU n).hom.f i ≫ (((o.finite n).toAdjunction.comp
